title: Chasing the Moon's Shadow
explanation:
# Eclipse from the Edge of Space

NASA's high-altitude WB-57F aircraft chased the Moon's shadow 50,000 feet above Iceland, capturing stunning views of the Sun's wispy corona (outer atmosphere) during a total solar eclipse on August 12, while planets like Venus and Jupiter became visible in the darkened daytime sky. Flying along the precisely calculated path of totality allowed the aircraft's powerful cameras to record the eclipse above clouds and atmospheric interference that would blur ground-based observations, revealing details impossible to see from below.
